Nairobi set for traffic changes as Harambee Stars face Zambia in CHAN 2024 clash

The National Police Service has issued a traffic advisory ahead of Sunday’s CHAN 2024 clash between Kenya’s Harambee Stars and Zambia’s Chipolopolo, warning motorists of temporary road closures and diversions across Nairobi. 

In a statement posted on X on Saturday, August 16, 2025, police detailed the affected routes and provided alternative paths to help ease traffic during the much-anticipated match. 

According to the advisory, Aerodrome Road from Madaraka Roundabout to Bunyala Roundabout will be closed, along with one lane of Lang’ata Road from Madaraka Roundabout to Lusaka Roundabout, and one lane of Mombasa Road from Lusaka Roundabout to Bunyala Roundabout. Motorists coming from Mombasa Road heading to the city center are advised to use Likoni Road through Enterprise Road or take the Southern Bypass via Ole Sereni. 

Those traveling from Lang’ata Road should use Raila Odinga Road or Muhoho Road via Mbagathi Roundabout. 

The statement also pointed out disruptions along Thika Superhighway and directed motorists to use Kiambu Road at Exit 4, the Northern Bypass, or Ruaka–Baba Ndogo–Lucky Summer–Nairobi River–Mwiki routes depending on their destination. 

Vehicles heading to Kasarani Stadium without access passes are required to use the Service Lane at Exit 7 or 8. 

Police assured the public that additional officers have been deployed and emphasized that stern action will be taken against anyone violating traffic rules. 

They urged drivers to cooperate with officers on duty to ensure safety and smooth traffic flow. 

The advisory comes as Harambee Stars, already through to the quarter-finals, look to secure the top spot in Group A. 

Fans have been encouraged to plan their travel early and follow the alternative routes provided to avoid congestion and arrive safely for the high-profile encounter.

data.raw_text:
Matagumpay na nailipat sa QCitizens Homes, Payatas Community 1, sa Milagrosa ang 14 pamilya na nakatira sa ibabaw ng tulay sa Brgy. Balon-Bato. Kasabay ito ng isinagawang joint clearing operation na naglalayong alisin ang mga ilegal na istruktura at matiyak ang kaligtasan at kaayusan sa lugar.

Bahagi ito ng mas pinaigting na kampanya ng Pamahalaang Lungsod sa pagpapatupad ng mga programa at operasyon kaugnay sa katiyakan sa paninirahan at kaayusan ng komunidad.

Nanguna sa operasyon ang Housing, Community Development and Resettlement Department (HCDRD), kasama ang QC Engineering Department (QCDE), Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS), Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD), Social Services Development Department (SSDD), Department of Sanitation and Cleanup Works (DSQC), City Legal Department, Task Force On Control, Prevention, and Removal Of Illegal Structures and Squatting (TF COPRISS), Task Force Disiplina, QCPD Station 3, at konseho ng barangay.

Katuwang din sa programa sina Chief of Staff Rowena Macatao, at District 6 Action Officer Atty. Mark Aldave.
